purpose: MODEL_CONTRACT.md task #26 — prove a TF.js port matches this pipeline.
nan_encoding: null (JSON has no NaN; a bare NaN token is invalid JSON)

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: centre_and_scale
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: shoulders (0.4,0.5)-(0.6,0.5) => mid (0.5,0.5), width 0.2; fill 0.25 -> -1.25 on x and y. Shoulders themselves land at -0.5 and +0.5, width 1 by construction.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: centre_and_scale_asymmetric
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: mid (0.5,0.5), width = hypot(0.4,0.16) — a diagonal shoulder line, which catches an implementation that takes |dx| instead of the Euclidean distance.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: left_shoulder_nan_DROPS_the_frame
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: Either shoulder missing => the frame cannot be placed in the training coordinate space at all, so live_demo.normalize returns None and the caller DROPS it. Keeping it and passing raw 0-1 pixel coords instead is silent out-of-distribution input.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: right_shoulder_nan_DROPS_the_frame
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: the mirror case, so neither side is special.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: zero_shoulder_width_DROPS_the_frame
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: width < 1e-6 => division would yield inf and the model would eat it. Dropped.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: nan_hand_is_PRESERVED_not_zeroed
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: An absent hand stays NaN. Substituting 0 places it at the shoulder midpoint — a real, plausible position — which is how 19,002 hand blocks once shipped as [0,0,0]. The model builds its own detection mask from NaN and then zeroes it internally.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: z_channel_passes_through_untouched
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: Normalization touches x,y only; the model drops z internally via PreprocessLayer(keep_z=False). A JS port that scales z too still 'works' and is silently off-contract.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: random_0
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: unstructured input — catches what the hand-built cases miss.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: random_1
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: unstructured input — catches what the hand-built cases miss.

stage1_and_2_normalize.name: random_2
stage1_and_2_normalize.why: unstructured input — catches what the hand-built cases miss.

properties.name: normalize_is_idempotent
properties.why: normalize(normalize(f)) == normalize(f). After one pass width is 1 and mid is the origin, so the second is a no-op. A frontend that normalizes twice is therefore still correct — do not 'fix' that by removing a needed call.

properties.name: normalized_shoulders_are_unit_apart_around_the_origin
properties.why: Whatever the input, after normalization the shoulder midpoint is (0,0) and the shoulder distance is 1. Two numbers a JS port can assert on its own output without any fixture at all.
